page.title: User guide
page.subtitle: Everything RBP Platform can do today, step by step, with screenshots from the live app.
page.howTo: Pick a chapter from the contents. Each one explains what the screen is for, who can use it and how to do the common tasks. Select any screenshot to see it full size.

roles.title: Who can do what
roles.intro: What each role can open. An owner can change which role a person has. Full means the person can view and make changes. Limited means they can view only, or use part of the area.
roles.pinNote: Some actions, such as discounts, removing items, voids, refunds and stock adjustments, also ask for an employee PIN. If the person's role isn't allowed to do the action, a manager enters their PIN to approve it.

comingSoon.title: Coming soon
comingSoon.intro: You can already see these screens in the menu, but they aren't finished yet. For now, they show a "coming soon" page.

orders.title: Sales → Orders
orders.body: A list of all past orders, where you can search them and reprint receipts.

staffReport.title: Reports → Staff
staffReport.body: Sales and hours for each staff member.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Business details, locations, users and roles, devices, payment methods, charges, printers, languages and modules.

start.title: Getting started
start.intro: How to sign in, pick the location you're working at, find your way around, and confirm sensitive actions with your employee PIN.

steps.open: Open the app. Enter your Email and Password, then select Sign in.
steps.location: If you work at more than one location, choose the one you're at today, for example Main Restaurant, and select Continue.
steps.home: The Dashboard opens. Kitchen staff go straight to the kitchen board instead.

steps.sidebar: Use the menu on the left. Select a group, for example Sales, to see its screens. You only see the screens your role can use.
steps.switchLocation: To change location, select the location name in the top bar and pick another one. Every screen then shows that location's data.
steps.phone: On a phone or small tablet, select the menu button at the top left to open the same menu.

pin.title: Confirm an action with your PIN
pin.intro: Each employee has their own 4-digit PIN, so the system records who did what.

steps.when: Sensitive actions, such as giving a discount, removing an item, a refund or a stock adjustment, open the Employee verification window.
steps.enter: Type your 4-digit PIN on the keypad or keyboard. The window shows which action you are approving.
steps.result: If your role is allowed to do it, the action goes ahead and is recorded under your name. If not, the message asks a manager to enter their PIN instead.

pin.note: Never share your PIN. Everything done with it is recorded in the audit log under your name.

steps.menu: Select your initials at the top right to open your account menu.
steps.language: Under Language, choose English, தமிழ் (Tamil) or සිංහල (Sinhala).
steps.signOut: Select Sign out when you finish, especially on a shared device.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: The home screen: a summary of today at the location you're signed in to.

steps.open: Select Dashboard at the top of the menu.
steps.cards: The cards show Sales today, Orders today, Average order and, at restaurants, Open tables and pending kitchen tickets.
steps.alerts: A yellow banner warns you when items are low or out of stock. Select View low stock to see which ones.
steps.shortcuts: Use the buttons at the top right, such as Open Restaurant POS or Open kitchen board, to jump straight to the screen you use most.

retailPos.title: Retail POS: make a sale
retailPos.intro: The Retail POS is the full-screen till for shop counters such as the Bakery Outlet. Cashiers, managers and owners use it to ring up items, add a customer, apply approved discounts and take payment. Open it from Sales → Retail POS while you are signed in to a shop location.

findProducts.title: Open the POS and find products
findProducts.intro: There are four ways to add an item: tap a tile, type in the search bar, open the full search, or scan a barcode.

steps.open: Open Sales → Retail POS. Product tiles are on the left and the Current sale is on the right. The location name at the top shows which shop you are selling for.
steps.tiles: Tap a category on the left, such as Bakery or Drinks, then tap a product tile to add one to the sale. Tap it again to add another. The tile shows how many are already in the sale, and a badge like 24 left warns when stock is low.
steps.search: To find an item by name or code, type in Search products or scan a barcode. Matching products appear as tiles. Press Enter to add the only match. Type a quantity first to add several at once, for example 3*B01 adds three of product B01.
steps.fullSearch: For a longer list, tap Search (or press F2). Filter by category, use the arrow keys to choose a product and press Enter to add it. Tap Done when you have finished.
steps.scan: To use a barcode scanner, scan the item while no box is being typed in. It goes straight into the sale. If the code is not sold at this shop, the POS tells you and nothing is added.

findProducts.note: You can't sell more than is in stock. If you try, the POS adds only what is left and tells you how many there are. Items marked unavailable can't be added.

buildCart.title: Change quantities and remove items

steps.select: Tap an item in the Current sale to open its controls.
steps.stepper: Tap + or − to change the quantity by one. On a keyboard, the + and − keys do the same for the selected item, and the arrow keys move between items.
steps.qty: To type a larger quantity, tap Qty, enter the number on the keypad and tap Set quantity.
steps.remove: To take an item off the sale, tap the red bin icon next to it, or press Delete on a keyboard.
steps.clear: To start again, tap Clear at the top of the sale and confirm. All items are removed.

buildCart.note: Items you have just added can be changed freely. Once a sale has been held, lowering or removing its saved items needs a manager's PIN and a reason (see Hold and resume a sale).

addCustomer.title: Add a customer to the sale
addCustomer.intro: A sale is for a Walk-in customer unless you add one. Adding a customer puts the sale on their history and lets you sell on credit.

steps.open: Tap Add customer at the top of the sale.
steps.phone: Type the customer's phone number in any format, such as 077…, 77… or +94…. When the customer is found, check the name and any amount they owe, then tap Select.
steps.name: If you don't have the number, type part of the name under Or search by name and select the right person.
steps.create: If no one has that number, fill in Customer name, and an address and Type if you want, then tap Create & select.
steps.remove: The customer's name now shows on the sale, with Owes if they have an unpaid balance. Tap the × next to the name to go back to a walk-in sale.

addCustomer.note: Only staff who are allowed to manage customers can create new ones. Others can still find existing customers or continue as walk-in.

discount.title: Give a discount or change a price
discount.intro: Discounts and price changes always need a manager's PIN and a reason. They are recorded in the audit log.

steps.open: Tap Discount under the total. Under Apply to, choose Whole bill or one item.
steps.value: Choose Percentage or Amount and enter the value on the keypad (or tap a quick choice such as 10%), or pick a ready-made offer under Promotion. Check the preview, for example Discount −LKR 117.00 · New total LKR 1,053.00, then tap Apply discount.
steps.pin: The Employee verification box opens. A manager enters their 4-digit PIN.
steps.reason: Choose the reason, such as Loyal customer, and tap Confirm. If you choose Other, type a comment. The discount appears in the sale totals.
steps.price: To change an item's price instead, tap the item, then Price. Enter the New unit price and tap Change price. A manager approves it with their PIN and a reason in the same way.

discount.note: Each shop has a highest discount a manager can approve here (50% by default). An amount discount can't be more than the bill or the item total. To take a bill discount off again, tap the × next to it in the totals.

steps.open: Tap Charges under the total.
steps.default: Tap a standard charge, for example Add LKR 30.00 for Packaging. Standard charges are added straight away and appear under On this sale.
steps.custom: For a different amount, tap Custom amount. For Other charge, also fill in What is it for?. Enter the amount and tap Add charge. A manager approves it with their PIN and a reason.
steps.remove: To remove a charge, tap the × next to it under On this sale or in the sale totals. Removing a charge also needs a manager's PIN and a reason.

takePayment.title: Take payment and give a receipt
takePayment.intro: Each sale is paid with one method. Split payments are not available.

steps.pay: Check the total and tap Pay. The Payment box shows the Amount due.
steps.cash: For cash, keep Cash selected. Tap Exact or a note amount, or type what the customer handed you. The POS shows the Change due, or Short by if it isn't enough.
steps.other: For Card, the customer taps, inserts or swipes the card on the terminal. For Bank transfer, type the Transfer reference from the slip. Credit sale adds the total to the customer's balance and only works when a customer is on the sale.
steps.take: Tap Take with the amount to finish the sale.
steps.receipt: The receipt opens. For cash, the Change due is shown at the top. Tap Print to send the receipt to the printer, then New sale to serve the next customer.

takePayment.note: If a payment doesn't go through, the sale is kept under its order number, so you can simply try again.

retailPosManage.title: Retail POS: held sales, returns and the drawer
retailPosManage.intro: Besides selling, the Retail POS lets you park a sale for later, look back at today's sales, reprint receipts, refund returned items and open the cash drawer. The Held and History buttons are next to the search bar in Sales → Retail POS.

holdSale.title: Hold and resume a sale
holdSale.intro: Hold a sale when a customer steps away, so you can serve the next person.

steps.hold: With items in the sale, tap Hold. Type a Label, such as the customer's name, and tap Hold sale. The sale is saved with an order number and the till is cleared.
steps.list: Tap Held to see the held sales at this shop. The number on the button shows how many are waiting.
steps.resume: Tap Resume next to the sale. The current sale must be empty first, so finish, hold or clear it.
steps.saved: The items on a resumed sale are marked Saved. You can add more freely, but lowering or removing a saved item needs a manager's PIN and a reason.
steps.cancel: To drop a held sale completely, resume it and tap Cancel sale. A manager enters their PIN and a reason. The sale is kept as cancelled, not deleted.

salesHistory.title: Find a sale, reprint a receipt or void a sale

steps.open: Tap History. It lists today's sales at this shop with their status and total.
steps.find: Search by Receipt number, customer or phone, or tap Paid, Held, Cancelled or Voided to filter.
steps.receipt: Tap Receipt to see the receipt again, then Print for a copy. Copies are marked REPRINT.
steps.void: To cancel a paid sale in full, tap Void. A manager enters their PIN and a reason. The full amount is refunded and the sale shows as Voided.

salesHistory.note: Only today's sales can be voided, and not once items have been returned. For those, use Return.

returnSale.title: Refund returned items

steps.open: Tap History, find the sale and tap Return.
steps.pick: Use + and − to choose how many of each item are coming back. You can't return more than was sold. The refund amount updates as you go.
steps.method: Under Refund to, choose Original payment or Cash. Keep Put returned items back in stock ticked if they can be sold again. Untick it to record them as wastage.
steps.approve: Tap Refund. A manager enters their PIN and chooses a reason, such as Customer returned item, then taps Confirm.
steps.receipt: A return receipt opens with its own number and the original sale number. Print it for the customer.

returnSale.note: The refund takes off each item's share of any discount on the original sale. You can return part of a sale now and the rest later, as long as it is still listed in History.

openDrawer.title: Open the cash drawer without a sale

steps.pin: Enter your PIN. Anyone allowed to open the drawer, including cashiers, can use their own PIN.
steps.reason: Choose why, such as Change for customer or Cash pickup, and tap Confirm. The drawer opens and the event is recorded in the audit log.

openDrawer.note: Cash put into or taken out of the drawer, and the count at the end of a shift, are recorded on the Cash drawer tab in Staff → Shifts.

restaurantTables.title: Tables and dine-in orders
restaurantTables.intro: The Tables screen is the restaurant floor plan. Waiters, managers and owners use it to see which tables are free, start a dine-in order, move a party to another table and print the bill. Open it from Sales → Tables while you are signed in to a restaurant location.

floorPlan.title: Read the floor plan

steps.open: Open Sales → Tables. Tables are grouped by area, such as Indoor, Outdoor and Bar, and each area heading shows how many of its tables are free.
steps.counts: The three boxes at the top count the tables that are Free, Occupied and Bill printed right now.
steps.tiles: Each table shows its name, number of seats and a status badge: green Free, purple Occupied or amber Bill printed. A busy table also shows its running total, how long ago the order was opened and who opened it.
steps.unsent: If a table shows a line like 2 not sent, it has items on the order that the kitchen hasn't received yet. Open the table and send them.

floorPlan.note: The Open POS button at the top right takes you straight to the sale screen without choosing a table.

openTable.title: Seat a table and send the order to the kitchen

steps.tap: On Sales → Tables, tap a Free table. The sale screen opens as a Dine-in order for that table, and the table name appears at the top of the sale.
steps.add: Tap a category, then tap products to add them. Each new item is marked Not sent until the kitchen has it.
steps.note: To add cooking instructions, tap the item in the sale, then tap Note. Tap a quick choice such as Less spicy or No onion, or type your own (up to 120 characters), then tap Save note. The note is printed on the kitchen ticket.
steps.send: Tap Send 5 to kitchen (the number is how many items are new). The order is saved and a kitchen ticket goes to each station that makes the food, such as the Main Kitchen and the Beverage Bar. Sent items change to Sent and the button reads All sent.
steps.leave: Tap Leave table when you are done. The order stays open on the table and the screen is free for the next table.
steps.more: When the table orders more, tap the table again, add the new items and tap Send to kitchen again. Only the new items go to the kitchen.

openTable.note: Items that don't need cooking, like short eats from the display, are saved on the order but don't create a kitchen ticket. Once an item has been sent, reducing or removing it needs a manager's PIN and a reason, and you choose what happens to the food. The kitchen then gets a cancel ticket.

transferTable.title: Move a party to another table
transferTable.intro: Use this when guests change tables after ordering. The whole order moves, together with its kitchen tickets.

steps.open: Tap the occupied table on Sales → Tables to open its order.
steps.transfer: Next to the table name, tap Transfer. Pick a Free table. Tables that are occupied can't be chosen.
steps.pin: A manager enters their PIN on the Employee verification keypad to approve the move.
steps.reason: Choose a reason, such as Customer request or Manager instruction, add a comment if you like, then tap Confirm.
steps.done: A message confirms the move, for example Moved T3 → T5. The kitchen tickets now show the new table, and the move is recorded in the audit log.

transferTable.note: Only a whole order can be moved, and only to a free table. Tables can't be merged, and a bill can't be split between tables.

printBill.title: Print the bill

steps.open: Tap the table on Sales → Tables to open its order.
steps.print: Tap Print bill. A bill marked BILL — NOT PAID opens, with the items, the service charge, tax and the total. Tap Print to print it, or Close.
steps.status: The table now shows Bill printed on the floor plan, so everyone can see it is waiting to pay.
steps.pay: When the guests pay, open the table and tap Pay. Payment works the same way as on the Retail POS, and the table becomes Free again.

printBill.note: If you add items after printing the bill, the table goes back to Occupied with the new total. Print a fresh bill before taking payment.

restaurantPos.title: Restaurant POS: takeaway and delivery
restaurantPos.intro: At a restaurant location the sale screen has order types for dine-in, takeaway and delivery, and it can send items to the kitchen. Cashiers, waiters, managers and owners use it. Open it from Sales → Restaurant POS.

steps.open: Open Sales → Restaurant POS. The order type buttons are at the top of the Current sale.
steps.dineIn: For Dine-in, tap Choose table and pick a free table. Until a table is chosen, the sale shows Choose a table for this dine-in order. and you can't send or pay.
steps.locked: Once an order has been saved (for example after sending it to the kitchen), its type can't be changed. A dine-in order can only change table with Transfer.

steps.add: Add the items. Add a note to an item if the customer asks, for example Parcel.
steps.send: Tap Send to kitchen. A message shows the kitchen ticket number and station, and the button changes to All sent.
steps.pay: Tap Pay and take the payment in the usual way. The customer's order is on the kitchen board as TAKEAWAY.

delivery.title: Take a phone order for delivery

steps.select: Add the items, then tap Delivery. The Delivery details window opens.
steps.phone: Type the customer's Phone first. If they are a saved customer, their name appears and the address fills in. For a new number, type the Address. Add Instructions (optional) such as a floor number or gate code.
steps.save: Tap Save. The address shows at the top of the sale, a saved customer is added to the sale, and the location's delivery charge is added to the total.
steps.send: Tap Send to kitchen. The order appears on Sales → Deliveries in Preparing.
steps.finish: If the customer pays now, tap Pay. If they will pay the rider, tap Hold and then Hold sale to clear the screen. The order stays on the Deliveries board marked Collect on delivery.

delivery.note: The address must be long enough to find the door. A short address shows a message asking for more detail. To change the details later, tap the address at the top of the sale.

steps.automatic: The location's service charge (10% at the Main Restaurant) is added automatically. It is worked out on the items after discounts and shows as Service charge (10%) in the totals.
steps.open: To see or change charges, tap Charges under the sale. The service charge shows 10% · automatic.
steps.change: To remove the service charge tap Waive, or tap Change rate and enter a new percentage. Both need a manager's PIN and a reason, and are recorded in the audit log.
steps.extra: To add a standard charge such as Packaging, tap its Add button. It is added at once, with no PIN. A Custom amount or removing a charge needs a manager's PIN.

kitchenBoard.title: Kitchen board (KOT)
kitchenBoard.intro: The kitchen board shows every kitchen order ticket (KOT) for your location on a full screen, so the chefs know what to cook next. Kitchen staff, managers and owners can move tickets along. Waiters can open it too, but only to look. Open it from Sales → KOT / Kitchen.

readBoard.title: Read the board

steps.open: Open Sales → KOT / Kitchen. Tickets sit in three columns: New, Preparing and Ready, with a count at the top of each. The board updates by itself every few seconds.
steps.ticket: Each ticket shows the order type and table in large letters (for example DINE-IN · T1, TAKEAWAY or DELIVERY), the ticket and order numbers, the items with any notes highlighted, the station and who sent it.
steps.timer: The clock on each ticket shows how long ago it arrived. A ticket still waiting after 15 minutes gets an amber border so it stands out.
steps.station: If you have more than one station, tap a station at the top, such as Main Kitchen or Beverage Bar, to see only its tickets. Tap All stations to see everything.

readBoard.note: When a new ticket arrives while the board is open, a short message such as 1 new ticket appears.

steps.start: When you start cooking, tap Start on the ticket. It moves to Preparing.
steps.ready: When the food is ready, tap Ready. It moves to Ready so the waiter or cashier can collect it.
steps.complete: When the food has left the kitchen, tap Served for a dine-in ticket or Picked up for takeaway and delivery. The ticket leaves the board.
steps.cancel: A red ticket marked Cancel means items were removed from an order after they were sent. It shows what should happen to the food. Read it, then tap Got it. Cancel tickets always appear at the top of their column.

steps.tap: Tap the printer button on the ticket.
steps.preview: The Kitchen ticket preview shows exactly what prints, and the name of the station's printer.
steps.again: Tap Print again to send it to that printer.

deliveries.title: Deliveries
deliveries.intro: The Deliveries board tracks every delivery order from the call to the door. Cashiers, managers and owners use it to confirm orders, send them to the kitchen and assign riders. Riders use it on their phones to see their own deliveries and collect payment. Open it from Sales → Deliveries.

steps.open: Open Sales → Deliveries. Today's delivery orders are grouped by stage: New, Confirmed, Preparing, Ready, Out for delivery and Delivered.
steps.card: Each card shows the order number, customer, total and whether it is Paid or Collect on delivery. It also shows the address, any instructions, the delivery charge, the rider (or No rider yet) and how long ago the order came in.
steps.filter: Use Date to look at another day, Rider to see one rider's orders, and the stage buttons to show just one stage.

moveOrder.title: Move an order through the stages
moveOrder.intro: The blue button on each card is always the next step.

steps.confirm: For a new phone order, tap Confirm once you have checked the details with the customer.
steps.kitchen: Tap Send to kitchen. The order moves to Preparing and a ticket appears on the kitchen board.
steps.ready: When the food is packed, tap Mark ready. Its kitchen ticket moves to Ready as well, so the kitchen doesn't cook it twice.

assignRider.title: Assign a rider

steps.choose: Pick a rider. Under each name you can see how many deliveries they have in hand and how many they are out on now, such as 2 active · 1 out now.
steps.assign: Tap Assign. The rider's name appears on the card, and the order shows on the rider's phone.
steps.change: To give the order to someone else before it leaves, tap Change rider.

assignRider.note: An order can't go Out for delivery until a rider is assigned.

riderRun.title: Deliver an order (rider, on a phone)

steps.open: Sign in on your phone, tap the menu button at the top left and open Sales → Deliveries. My deliveries lists only the orders assigned to you.
steps.out: When you leave with the food, tap Out for delivery on the order.
steps.delivered: At the door, tap Delivered. If the order is already Paid, it is marked delivered straight away.
steps.collect: If the card says Collect on delivery, the Collect payment window opens with the amount to collect. Choose Cash or Card. For cash, enter the Cash received, and the change to give back is shown.
steps.confirm: Tap Paid · delivered. The payment is recorded and the order moves to Delivered.

riderRun.note: Riders can only mark their own orders out for delivery and delivered. If the cash received is less than the total, the window shows Not enough cash and won't let you finish.

deliveryDetail.title: See a delivery's details and print a dispatch slip

steps.open: Tap an order number on the board. The page shows the phone, rider, address and instructions, the items with the delivery charge and total, and how much is to be collected.
steps.progress: The Progress list on the right shows each stage with the time and the person who moved it.
steps.slip: Tap Dispatch slip to print a slip for the rider with the address and PAID or the amount to collect.

deliveryDetail.note: The next step buttons, such as Out for delivery, are also on this page. A rider can only open the deliveries assigned to them.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.intro: The catalog holds everything you sell: products, the categories they sit in, where each one is sold, its price at each location and how the buttons are laid out on the POS Quick Pad. Find it under Catalog in the sidebar. Everyone at the till can look up products; owners and managers make the changes.

findProduct.title: Find and edit a product
findProduct.intro: The product list covers your whole business. Prices and availability for each location are set separately.

steps.open: Open Catalog → Products. Each row shows the code, name, category, Base price, Tax mode and whether the product is on the Quick Pad.
steps.search: Type in Search name, code or barcode to find a product quickly. You can also scan a barcode into this box.
steps.filter: Pick a category in All categories to see only that category and its subcategories. Use Active or Inactive to narrow the list further.
steps.openProduct: Click a product to open it. The Where it's sold card on the right shows each location that sells it and the price there, with Manage locations and Edit prices shortcuts.
steps.save: Change what you need and click Save. To stop selling a product everywhere, turn off Active. It disappears from the POS and pickers, but its sales history is kept.

findProduct.note: Cashiers and waiters can browse the list but can't open or change products. Only owners and managers can edit the catalog.

addProduct.title: Add a new product

steps.open: Open Catalog → Products and click New product.
steps.details: Fill in Name, Code (your SKU or PLU) and Category. A Description is optional.
steps.translations: Under Names in other languages, add the Tamil and Sinhala names if you want them shown on the POS and receipts. If you leave them blank, the English name is shown.
steps.price: Enter the Base price, then choose the Tax mode: Inclusive means the price already includes tax, and Exclusive means tax is added at checkout.
steps.barcodes: To add a barcode, scan it into the Barcodes box or type it and press Enter (or click Add barcode). You can add more than one barcode. Click the × on a barcode to remove it.
steps.options: Optionally, use Upload image to add a picture for the POS button. Leave Show on Quick Pad on if the product should have its own button. With it off, staff can still sell the product by searching or scanning.
steps.save: Click Save. The product is created for the whole business. Next, choose which locations sell it in Location Products.

addProduct.note: The code must be unique in your business, and the base price must be more than zero. A barcode can belong to only one product, so if another product already uses it, the app tells you and won't save.

categories.title: Organise categories
categories.intro: Categories group your products on the POS, on receipts and in reports. A category can have subcategories, for example Drinks → Hot Drinks.

steps.open: Open Catalog → Categories. Subcategories are shown indented under their parent category.
steps.new: Click New category, then enter a Name and Code.
steps.parent: To make it a subcategory, choose a Parent category. Leave it empty for a top-level category. Sort order is optional. Lower numbers come first.
steps.colour: Under Appearance, pick the button Colour for the Quick Pad. You can also add Tamil and Sinhala names and a Button image.
steps.manage: To change an existing category, click the ⋮ menu on its row, then choose Edit, Add subcategory or Deactivate.

categories.note: A deactivated category is hidden from the POS and pickers, but its products and history are kept. You can't deactivate a category that still has active subcategories or products. Move or deactivate them first.

locationProducts.title: Choose what each location sells
locationProducts.intro: Each location sells its own selection of products. Only owners and managers can open this screen.

steps.open: Open Catalog → Location Products. Products are grouped by category.
steps.location: Choose the location in the drop-down at the top right. The summary line shows how many products are sold there.
steps.soldHere: Turn Sold here on or off for each product. Products that aren't sold here are greyed out. Use the Sold here and Not sold filters to check your list.
steps.available: If an item runs out for the day, turn Available off. Its button stays on the POS, but it is greyed out.
steps.stockNote: Type a short Stock note such as "4 left" and press Enter. The note shows on the product's POS button at this location.
steps.settings: Click the settings button at the end of a row to choose the Kitchen station where its KOT prints and to set whether Service charge applies when it is sold here.

locationProducts.note: The price column shows the price at this location. A Location price tag means it differs from the base price. Change it in Pricing.

pricing.title: Set prices for each location
pricing.intro: One grid shows the base price for every product plus a column for each location. Only owners and managers can open it.

steps.open: Open Catalog → Pricing. Use the search box or All categories to find the products you want.
steps.edit: Type a new price in the Base price column or in a location column. Changed cells are highlighted, and the bar at the bottom counts the unsaved changes. If a change makes a price lower, the bar shows Lower than before.
steps.useBase: An empty location cell uses the base price, shown in grey. To remove a location price, clear its cell. A cell marked Not sold here is for a product that location doesn't sell.
steps.save: Click Save changes to save them all at once, or Discard to undo them.
steps.approve: If any price goes down, a manager enters their PIN. Then choose a reason, such as Price correction, and click Confirm.

pricing.note: Price cuts always need a manager's PIN and a reason, and they are recorded in the audit log. Staff who can see the audit report also get a Recent price changes panel showing each change as old → new.

quickPad.title: Arrange the Quick Pad
quickPad.intro: The Quick Pad is the grid of category and product buttons on the POS. Each location can have its own order and colours.

steps.open: Open Catalog → Quick Pad Setup.
steps.choose: Pick the location at the top. Leave All devices at this location selected, or pick a single POS terminal or tablet to give it a layout of its own.
steps.reorder: Drag the category buttons into the order you want, or use the up and down arrows. Click a category to see its Buttons in list, then reorder the products in the same way.
steps.drill: Click the › arrow on a category to open its subcategories. Click Top level to go back up.
steps.colour: Click the coloured dot next to a category to choose its button colour at this location. Click Use category colour to go back to the colour set for the category.
steps.save: Check the Live preview below, then click Save. Click Discard to undo.

quickPad.note: A device with its own layout shows a notice with a Use location layout button that switches it back. Products with Show on Quick Pad turned off, and products not sold at the location, don't appear here.

customers.title: Customers
customers.intro: Keep one customer list for the whole business, with phone numbers, addresses, order history and money owed on credit. Open Customers → Customers. Cashiers, owners and managers can add and edit customers. Waiters can view them.

findCustomer.title: Find a customer

steps.open: Open Customers → Customers. The cards at the top show Total outstanding (how much customers owe across all locations) and the number of customers.
steps.search: Type a name or phone number in the search box. Phone numbers match however they are typed, with or without spaces.
steps.filter: Filter by type (Walk-in / retail, Regular, Corporate) or tap Owes money. Use the sort menu to show Recent orders first or Highest balance first.
steps.openCustomer: Click a customer to open their page.

findCustomer.note: If you search for a phone number that no customer has, the app offers Create customer with this number, with the number already filled in.

addCustomer.title: Add a customer

steps.open: Open Customers → Customers and click New customer.
steps.phones: Enter a phone number. Click Add another number for each extra number they call from, and give each a Label such as Mobile or Home.
steps.primary: Select Primary next to the main number. The primary number is printed on receipts and deliveries.
steps.address: Optionally add an Address and Notes. Untick Deliver to the same address if deliveries go somewhere else, then fill in the Delivery address.

addCustomer.note: A phone number can belong to only one customer. If it's already taken, a warning shows who has it, with a link to open that customer.

steps.overview: On the customer's page, the Overview tab shows the number of orders, Total spent, the Last order date, the Outstanding balance and their Recent orders.
steps.orders: Open the Order history tab to see every order from every location. Use the status chips, such as Paid or Voided, to filter the list.
steps.orderDetail: Click an order to see its items, charges, total, how it was paid and who served it.
steps.edit: To update phone numbers, addresses or notes, click Edit at the top right.

receivePayment.title: Take a payment on a customer's account
receivePayment.intro: When a customer buys on credit, the amount is added to their balance. Record it here when they pay it back.

steps.open: Open the customer, go to the Balance tab and click Receive payment. The tab lists every credit sale, return and payment as an Account statement.
steps.method: Under Paid by, choose Cash, Card or Bank transfer. For a bank transfer, enter the Transfer reference.
steps.amount: Enter the amount on the keypad, or tap Full balance. Balance after payment shows what they will still owe.
steps.confirm: Click Receive. The payment gets a number, appears in the statement and reduces the Current balance.

receivePayment.note: You can't take more than the customer owes. Payments can be taken by staff who handle the cash drawer or manage customers.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.intro: Inventory shows how much of each item you have at every location, and records every change to it: sales, transfers, deliveries, wastage and adjustments. Find it in the Inventory menu. Anyone with inventory access can look up stock. Owners and managers can adjust stock, and owners, managers and field sales reps can transfer it.

checkStock.title: Check stock on hand
checkStock.intro: See how much you have of each item at a location, and which items are running low.

steps.open: Open Inventory → Stock. The cards at the top show how many items are tracked, and how many are Low stock or Out of stock at your location.
steps.filter: Type in Item name or code to find an item. Use the location list to look at another location, or choose All locations to see every location at once. You can also narrow the list by category.
steps.status: Tap Low stock or Out of stock to see only those items. Tap All to see everything again.
steps.openItem: Tap an item to open its stock page. It has a card for each location with the amount On hand, its minimum and its status.
steps.recent: Scroll down to Recent movements to see the latest sales, transfers and adjustments for the item. Tap All movements to see its full history.

checkStock.note: An item shows as Low stock when it is at or below its minimum, and Out of stock when none is left. Out of stock items can't be sold.

adjustStock.title: Adjust stock
adjustStock.intro: Correct the stock after a count, or record items that were found, damaged, spoiled or eaten by staff.

steps.open: Open Inventory → Stock (or Inventory → Adjustments) and tap Adjust stock. From an item's stock page you can also tap Adjust on a location card.
steps.pickItem: Check the location, then search for the item and tap it.
steps.kind: Choose the type of adjustment: Stock count, Add stock, Remove stock, Wastage or Staff meal. Then tap Next.
steps.quantity: Enter the quantity on the keypad. For a Stock count, enter what you counted and the app works out the difference. Check Stock after, then tap Continue to approval.
steps.pin: A manager enters their 4-digit PIN to approve the change.
steps.reason: Choose why the stock is changing, for example Stock count difference or Expired, and tap Confirm. If you choose Other, add a comment.
steps.history: Open Inventory → Adjustments to see every adjustment, with the change, the reason and who approved it.

adjustStock.note: Every adjustment needs a manager's PIN and a reason, and is kept in the audit log. You can't take stock below zero, and a count that matches the stock on hand has nothing to adjust.

transferStock.title: Send stock to another location
transferStock.intro: Move stock between your locations, for example from the Central Store to the Bakery Outlet.

steps.open: Open Inventory → Transfers and tap New transfer.
steps.locations: Check From (where the stock leaves) and choose To (where it goes).
steps.items: Search for an item and tap it, then set how many to send. Tap Add item to add more items. You can only send what is available at the sending location.
steps.note: Add a Note (optional) for the person receiving it, such as the delivery run.
steps.dispatch: Tap Dispatch. The transfer appears in the list as In transit, and the stock leaves the sending location straight away.
steps.cancel: Made a mistake? At the sending location, open the transfer while it is still In transit and tap Cancel transfer. The items go back into stock at the sender.

receiveTransfer.title: Receive a transfer
receiveTransfer.intro: When the stock arrives, the receiving location counts it in so it is added to their stock.

steps.switch: Make sure you are working at the receiving location. If not, tap the location name at the top of the screen and choose it.
steps.incoming: Open Inventory → Transfers, tap Incoming, and tap the transfer that is In transit.
steps.check: Check each item against what arrived. If something is missing, change the quantity to what you actually received. The app shows how many are short.
steps.receive: Tap Receive all, or Receive (… short) if something was missing. The transfer changes to Received and the stock is added at your location.

receiveTransfer.note: Only the receiving location can receive a transfer, and only the sending location can cancel it. Any shortage is recorded on the transfer.

movements.title: Look up stock movements
movements.intro: The stock movements list is the history of every change to stock: sales, returns, transfers, deliveries, production, wastage, staff meals and adjustments.

steps.open: Open Inventory → Stock Movement. The newest movements are at the top.
steps.filter: Narrow the list by location and by type (for example Transfer in or Adjustment), and pick a time range: Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.
steps.read: Each row shows the item, the location, the type and the quantity (minus when stock goes out). Reference shows the sale, transfer, delivery or adjustment number, and By shows who did it.
steps.fromItem: To see one item's history only, open the item from Inventory → Stock and tap All movements.

lowStock.title: Deal with low stock
lowStock.intro: The Low Stock page lists every item that is at or below its minimum, grouped by location, so you can top it up.

steps.open: Open Inventory → Low Stock. Each item shows how many are on hand, its minimum and how far below the minimum it is.
steps.minimum: To change when an item counts as low, tap Minimum, set the new level and tap Save minimum. Set it to 0 to turn the alert off.
steps.transferIn: Tap Transfer in to fill it up from another location. A new transfer opens from the location with the most stock, with a suggested quantity. Check it and tap Dispatch.
steps.adjust: If the stock number is wrong, tap Adjust to correct it. This needs a manager's PIN and a reason.

lowStock.note: To order more from a supplier instead, create a purchase order (see Purchasing).

purchasing.title: Purchasing
purchasing.intro: Purchasing is where you keep your suppliers, order stock from them and check deliveries in. Goods you receive are added to stock straight away. Find it in the Purchasing menu. It is available to owners and managers.

suppliers.title: Add a supplier

steps.open: Open Purchasing → Suppliers. The list shows each supplier's contact, open orders, last order and how much you have received from them.
steps.fill: Enter the Supplier name and the Payment terms (days), where 0 means cash on delivery. Add the contact person, phone, email, address and a note if you have them.
steps.save: Tap Save supplier. The supplier's page opens, where you can start a New purchase order for them or tap Edit to change their details.
steps.deactivate: If you stop buying from a supplier, tap Deactivate on their page and confirm. They can't be chosen on new orders, but orders already placed can still be received. Tap Reactivate to use them again.

suppliers.note: Only the supplier name is required.

createPo.title: Create a purchase order

steps.open: Open Purchasing → Purchase Orders and tap New purchase order.
steps.supplier: Choose the Supplier. Check Deliver to (your current location is filled in), and set the Expected delivery date and a Note if you need them.
steps.items: Tap Add item, search for an item and tap it. Add as many items as you need, then tap Done adding.
steps.costs: Set the quantity and the Unit cost for each item. The last cost you paid is filled in for you. The Order summary shows the number of items, units and the Total.
steps.save: Tap Place order to send it now, or Save as draft to check it later.

createPo.note: Every item needs a quantity and a unit cost. Inactive suppliers can't be chosen.

placePo.title: Place, track or cancel an order

steps.open: Open Purchasing → Purchase Orders and tap the order. A draft shows Draft — not sent yet.
steps.edit: To change a draft, tap Edit, make your changes and save it again. Once an order is placed it can no longer be edited.
steps.place: When the items and costs are right, tap Place order. The status changes to Ordered.
steps.track: Back in the list, use the status and supplier filters to follow your orders. Orders show Part received while some items are still to come, and Overdue when the expected date has passed.
steps.cancel: To cancel an order that hasn't been delivered yet, tap Cancel order, enter a Reason and confirm. Tell the supplier separately.

placePo.note: You can only cancel an order while nothing has been received against it.

receiveGoods.title: Receive goods from a supplier
receiveGoods.intro: When a delivery arrives, check it in against its purchase order so the stock goes up.

steps.open: Open Purchasing → Goods Receiving. Awaiting delivery lists every order that is still to come.
steps.receive: Tap Receive next to the order. You can also tap Receive goods on the order itself.
steps.count: Each item is filled in with the quantity still to come. If less arrived, change it to what you actually received. The app shows the stock now and after this delivery.
steps.invoice: Enter the Supplier invoice no. from the delivery note, and add a Note if something was wrong.
steps.submit: Tap Receive … units. The goods received note (GRN) opens, and each item is added to stock as a Purchase movement. Tap Stock movements to see them.

receiveGoods.note: If only part of the order arrives, the rest stays on the order as Part received, and you can receive it when it comes. You can't receive more than is still to come.

recipesKitchen.title: Recipes & kitchen prep
recipesKitchen.intro: Set up the ingredients your kitchen counts, say what one plate of each dish uses, plan the day's ingredient needs and look after cooked food waiting to be resold. Owners and managers use all of it from Production in the sidebar; kitchen staff use Production → Prepared Items.

ingredients.title: Keep your ingredient list up to date
ingredients.intro: Ingredients are stock-only items that are never sold on the POS. Each one is counted in portions, pieces or packs.

steps.open: Open Production → Ingredients. The cards at the top show how many ingredients this location tracks and how many are Low or out.
steps.read: Check each row: One portion is says what the kitchen weighs or counts out, On hand is the current stock, and Status turns to low or out of stock at or below the Minimum. Click a row to see every stock movement for that ingredient.
steps.edit: Click the pencil next to an ingredient to edit it, or click New ingredient to add one. Fill in Name, Code, Counted in, Minimum at this location and One portion is.
steps.save: Add Grams per portion and Portions per pack if you know them, then click Save ingredient.
steps.orderLow: To restock, click Order the low ones under the Low or out card. A new purchase order opens with the low ingredients already on it.

ingredients.note: A code and a name are required, and two ingredients can't share a name. If you enter grams or portions per pack, you must also describe the portion.

recipe.title: Set up a recipe
recipe.intro: A recipe says what one plate of a dish uses. Once it is on, each sale takes those ingredients out of kitchen stock.

steps.open: Open Production → Recipes and scroll to Menu items without a recipe.
steps.add: Click Add recipe next to the dish. You can also click New recipe at the top and choose the dish under Menu item.
steps.ingredients: Under One plate uses, pick an ingredient in Choose an ingredient and click Add ingredient. Repeat for each ingredient and set how many portions or pieces one plate takes. The Preview on the right shows how many can be made here right now.
steps.deduct: Leave Deduct ingredients when sold on so the dish is made to order. Turn it off to pause the recipe: sales then leave the ingredients alone and the dish is counted as finished stock again.
steps.save: Add a Note if it helps the kitchen, then click Save recipe. To change a recipe later, click its row in the Recipes list.

recipe.note: A recipe needs a menu item and at least one ingredient before it can be saved.

canMake.title: Check how many dishes can be made

steps.open: Open Production → Recipes.
steps.read: Read the Can make column. It is how many plates the scarcest ingredient allows at this location, and limited by names that ingredient.
steps.ready: The Ready column shows cooked plates waiting in Prepared Items. They are included in Can make.
steps.location: Use the location box above the list to check another location.

canMake.note: A 0 shown in red means the dish can't be made until the limiting ingredient is restocked.

portions.title: Plan today's ingredient needs

steps.open: Open Production → Portions & Planning. Portion definitions lists what one portion of each ingredient is. Click Edit on a row to change it.
steps.expected: Scroll to Today's requirement. Under Expected sales today, each dish starts at its average for the last 30 days. Change the numbers to match what you expect to sell today.
steps.read: Read Ingredients needed: Need is expected plates times the recipe, Have is what's in the kitchen, and Buy is the difference. When portions per pack are set, it also suggests how many packs to buy.
steps.order: Click Create purchase order to open a purchase order with the items to buy already filled in.

portions.note: If nothing is short, the page says there's enough in the kitchen for the expected sales, and no order button appears.

prepared.title: Resell or dispose of prepared food
prepared.intro: Cooked food from a cancelled order, or food made extra, waits here. The next order for the same item uses it before a new one is cooked.

steps.open: Open Production → Prepared Items. Each card shows the dish, when it was prepared and by whom, and how long is left under Sell by.
steps.filter: Use the chips to show Ready to sell, Expired, Sold or Disposed items, or All.
steps.add: To add food made ahead, click Add prepared item, choose the Menu item, set the Quantity and Sell within (hours), then click Add to the queue.
steps.dispose: If a plate can't be resold, click Dispose on its card. Choose what happened: Wastage, Staff meal, Disposed or Other.
steps.confirm: Type a Reason and click Dispose. The reason is kept in the audit log.

prepared.note: Kitchen staff can see the queue and dispose of items. Only owners and managers can add prepared items. Adding a dish that has a recipe takes its ingredients from stock straight away.

bakeryProduction.title: Bakery production
bakeryProduction.intro: Plan what the bakery bakes each day, run each batch from raw materials to finished goods, and keep track of what is wasted. Owners and managers find it under Production in the sidebar, from Bakery Production to Wastage.

steps.open: Open Production → Bakery Production. How production works shows the order of work: plan the day, start a batch, record output, and finished goods go into stock.
steps.shortage: If a raw material is short for today's plan, a yellow warning names it. Click Order what's short to open a purchase order for it.
steps.tiles: The cards show Produced / planned today, Batches baking now, Wastage (7 days) and Finished goods low.
steps.batches: Scroll down to see today's batches, with Start and Record output buttons, and a Last 7 days table of units baked and wasted.

plan.title: Plan a day's baking

steps.open: Open Production → Production Plan and click New plan.
steps.details: Check the Production location and Plan date (tomorrow is filled in for you), and add a Note if you like.
steps.quantities: Under What to bake, enter how many of each product you need. Batches are whole runs of the formula, so the app rounds up and shows how many runs and how many units to expect. Raw materials needed shows what the plan uses and anything that is short.
steps.save: Click Save draft. A draft can still be changed with Edit.
steps.confirm: Click Confirm plan. The plan creates one batch for each product, listed under Batches and ready to start.

plan.note: A plan needs at least one product. Once confirmed, it can't be edited. To stop it, use Cancel plan and give a reason: batches that haven't started are cancelled too.

startBatch.title: Start a batch

steps.open: Open Production → Production Batches. Use the chips to show Planned, Baking, Completed or Cancelled batches.
steps.used: Check each raw material. Used starts at the Formula amount; change it to what was actually used.
steps.confirm: Click Start batch. The raw materials leave stock now and the batch shows as Baking.

startBatch.note: If you enter more than is on hand, a warning says there's not enough in stock and the batch can't start until the material is received.

recordOutput.title: Record a batch's output

steps.open: When the batch comes out of the oven, click Record output on its row.
steps.counts: Enter the Good units and the number Rejected.
steps.reason: If anything was rejected, choose a reason under Why rejected and add a comment if needed. The line at the bottom shows how many go into stock and how many go to wastage.
steps.confirm: Click Record output. Good units go into finished goods and rejects are recorded as wastage.
steps.detail: Click the batch row to open it. You can see its progress, the raw materials used, the good and rejected units, and every stock movement.

recordOutput.note: A reason is required when anything is rejected. The Other reason also needs a comment. A batch that hasn't started can be cancelled from its page with a reason.

steps.open: Open Production → Finished Goods. The cards show the total On hand, Produced today and how many products are Low or out.
steps.read: Each row shows stock on hand against its minimum, Produced today, Wasted today and the Last batch.
steps.transfer: To send goods to a shop, click Stock & transfer. This opens the product's stock page, where you can make the transfer.

wastage.title: Write off goods and review wastage

steps.writeOff: On Finished Goods, click Write off on a product. You can also use Write off at the top of the Wastage page. Enter the Quantity to write off, add a Note, then click Write off.
steps.pin: A manager enters their PIN to approve.
steps.reason: Choose why the goods are being written off, for example Expired or Damaged item, then click Confirm. Stock drops by that amount.
steps.review: Open Production → Wastage. It lists batch rejects and write-offs, with the reason, source, who recorded it and who approved it with their PIN. By reason totals each reason.
steps.filter: Use Today, 7 days or 30 days, the Batch reject and Written off chips, or click a reason to narrow the list. The total wasted is shown at the bottom.

wastage.note: You can't write off more than is on hand. Only someone allowed to manage production can approve a write-off with their PIN.

wholesaleShops.title: External shops
wholesaleShops.intro: External shops are the wholesale customers your van sells to on credit. Here you see what each shop owes, how close it is to its credit limit, and its full history. Open it from Customers → External Shops.

findShop.title: Find a shop and see what it owes

steps.open: Open Customers → External Shops. Each row shows the shop, its route and stop number, its phone, what it owes against its credit limit, and the last visit.
steps.totals: The cards at the top show the number of Shops, the total Owed to you, and how much is Overdue, with the number of shops over their limit.
steps.filter: Use the chips Owes money, Overdue or Over limit to narrow the list, or pick a route in All routes. Type a shop name, owner or area in the search box to find one shop.
steps.openShop: Click a shop to open its page.

findShop.note: A shop is Overdue when part of an invoice is still unpaid after the shop's payment terms. The coloured bar turns amber as the shop gets close to its credit limit.

statement.title: Check a shop's statement and balance

steps.header: The top of the shop page shows what it owes (Outstanding) against its credit limit, its Payment terms, phone, route and stop, address and notes.
steps.read: The Statement tab lists every invoice, collection and return, newest first, with the running Balance after each one. An invoice adds only the part that was not paid at the time of sale; collections and returns reduce the balance.
steps.tabs: Use the Invoices, Collections and Returns tabs to see each kind of document on its own. Click an invoice or return number to open it.
steps.actions: Use the buttons at the top to act for this shop: New sale, Collect payment, Record return or Edit shop.

statement.note: A red Over the credit limit banner means you should collect a payment before giving more credit. New sale only shows for people who work on the van that serves this shop.

addShop.title: Add a new shop

steps.open: On External Shops, click New shop.
steps.route: Pick the Route the van uses to reach the shop, or leave No route.
steps.credit: Set the Credit limit and the Payment terms in days (up to 120). Add any Notes, such as opening days.
steps.save: Click Save shop. The new shop's page opens.

addShop.note: Shops are wholesale customers only. They don't appear on the POS.

wholesaleRoutes.title: Routes
wholesaleRoutes.intro: A route is the list of shops a van visits on set days, in stop order. The route overview shows the day's progress and what is left in the van. Open it from Wholesale → Routes.

steps.open: Open Wholesale → Routes. The route that runs today opens on its own, with its rep's name under the title.
steps.pick: To see another route or day, change Route or Date. If the route doesn't normally run on that day, a note tells you.
steps.totals: The cards show Stops visited, Sales (with how much went On credit), Cash taken (cash at sale plus collections) and Returns.
steps.stops: The stops are listed in visiting order. A green Visited badge shows what was sold and collected there; To visit means the stop is still waiting.
steps.act: At a stop, tap Sell to start a sale to that shop, or Collect to take a payment. Tap the shop name to open its page.

vanStock.title: Check and load the van

steps.check: The On Van card beside the stops shows how many of each product are left in the van. A number in red means that item has run out.
steps.load: To load more stock, click Load the van (transfer). It opens Inventory → Transfers, where you move stock from the store to the van.

vanStock.note: Load the van (transfer) only appears for people allowed to make stock transfers.

fieldSales.title: Field sales
fieldSales.intro: The field sales screen is where the rep sells to a shop from the van, usually on a phone. The goods come out of the van's stock, and the shop can pay now, later on credit, or part of each. Open it from Wholesale → Field Sales.

sell.title: Sell to a shop from the van

steps.open: Open Wholesale → Field Sales. Under Which shop?, the shops on Today's route come first, with what each one owes. Tap the shop you are at.
steps.goods: Under Goods from the van, enter how many of each item the shop takes, or use + and −. Each item shows its wholesale price and how many are in the van.
steps.review: Check the item count and total in the bar at the bottom, then tap Review.
steps.payment: Under Payment, enter what the shop pays now in Paid now, or tap Paid in full or All on credit. If money is paid, choose Paid by: Cash, Bank transfer or Cheque. Check On credit and the shop's New balance.
steps.create: Tap Create invoice. The invoice opens, ready to give to the shop.

sell.note: You can't sell more than is in the van. If the sale takes the shop over its credit limit, you see a warning and must tick Continue anyway; the invoice is then flagged as sold over the limit. Wholesale prices include VAT. Selling needs access to a van: a manager at a shop sees Selling needs a van instead, but can still see shops and take collections.

share.title: Give the shop its invoice

steps.invoice: The invoice shows the items, the total with VAT, what was paid now and what is On credit, the Due date, and the shop's Previous balance and Balance now.
steps.print: Under Give the shop a copy, tap Print to print it on the receipt printer. Once printed, the button becomes Reprint.
steps.send: To send it instead, tap WhatsApp to message it to the shop's number, Share (on phones that support it), or Copy text to paste it anywhere.
steps.next: Tap Next sale to go back to the shop list, or Record a return if the shop hands goods back against this invoice.

share.note: Every print and share is recorded on the invoice with who did it and when.

wholesaleCollections.title: Collections
wholesaleCollections.intro: A collection is money a shop pays towards what it owes. It is applied to the shop's oldest unpaid invoices first. See all collections in Wholesale → Collections.

collect.title: Collect a payment from a shop

steps.open: Tap Collect next to a stop on Wholesale → Routes, click Collect payment on the shop's page, or on Wholesale → Collections click Collect and choose the shop.
steps.method: The window shows what the shop owes. Choose Paid by: Cash, Bank transfer or Cheque.
steps.amount: Enter the Amount. It starts at the full balance. For a bank transfer or cheque, also enter the Transfer reference or Cheque number.
steps.confirm: Check Balance after, then click the Collect button, which shows the amount.

collect.note: You can't collect more than the shop owes. Collect is greyed out for a shop that owes nothing.

steps.open: Open Wholesale → Collections. The cards show how much was collected in the period and how much shops Still owe.
steps.filter: Choose Today, 7 days or 30 days, and pick a route to see only its shops.
steps.applied: Each row shows the shop, the date, how it was paid, and under Applied to which invoices the money paid off.

wholesaleReturns.title: Returns from shops
wholesaleReturns.intro: When a shop gives goods back, record a return. The shop is credited, good stock goes back into the van, and anything damaged, expired or spoiled is written off as wastage. Open it from Wholesale → Returns.

record.title: Record a return

steps.open: Open Wholesale → Returns and click New return. You can also use Record return on the shop's page or Record a return on an invoice.
steps.shop: Choose the Shop. Under From invoice, pick the invoice the goods came from, or leave Not linked to an invoice.
steps.items: Enter how many of each item came back and set its condition: Good — resell, Damaged, Expired or Wastage. The Credit to the shop panel shows the credit and the shop's new balance.
steps.pin: Click Record return. An employee who is allowed to accept shop returns enters their PIN.
steps.reason: Choose why the shop is returning goods, add a comment if needed, and click Confirm.

record.note: When you pick an invoice, you can't return more than was sold on it (the most is shown as "up to"). Items that are not in good condition are recorded as wastage.

steps.list: Wholesale → Returns lists returns for Today, 7 days or 30 days, with the items, their condition, the invoice and the credit.
steps.detail: Click a return to open it. It shows the Credit, the shop's Balance afterwards, the Invoice, the Reason with who approved it by PIN, and which van the goods went Back into.
steps.movements: Scroll down to Stock movements to see how each item was booked into the van's stock.

staffEmployees.title: Employees
staffEmployees.intro: The employee list shows your staff, where they work, who is clocked in now, and how much of their food allowance they have used this month. Owners and managers open it from Staff → Employees.

steps.open: Open Staff → Employees.
steps.search: Type a name, employee code, job title or phone in the search box, or pick a location to see only its staff.
steps.read: The Status column shows who is in now and where. Meals this month turns red when someone has eaten more than their allowance.

steps.open: Click an employee. The page shows their phone, the locations they work at (Works at), their Sign-in and when they Joined.
steps.allowance: The Food allowance this month card shows what they have eaten against their allowance. Anything over it is marked for salary deduction.
steps.tabs: The Attendance tab lists their clock-ins and clock-outs with hours. Staff meals this month lists their meals.
steps.edit: Click Edit to change their details, set a new PIN, or turn off Active when someone leaves.

add.title: Add an employee

steps.open: On Staff → Employees, click Add employee.
steps.details: Enter the Name, Job title, Phone and Monthly food allowance.
steps.pin: Enter a 4-digit PIN. Staff use it to clock in and to approve actions. Each PIN must be different from everyone else's.
steps.locations: Under Works at, tick every location this person works at.

add.note: Only owners and managers with permission to manage staff see Add employee and Edit.

staffAttendance.title: Attendance
staffAttendance.intro: Staff clock in and out with their PIN on a shared device, and the attendance sheet compares that with the roster. Open it from Staff → Attendance.

clock.title: Clock in or out

steps.open: Open Staff → Attendance on the shared device at the location.
steps.pin: In the Clock in / out panel, the employee taps their 4-digit PIN. Use Clear or the delete key to fix a mistake.
steps.result: The panel confirms who clocked in, or who clocked out and how long they worked. If they're more than 10 minutes late for their shift, it says so.

clock.note: The same PIN clocks you in, or out if you're already in. Staff can only clock in at a location they work at.

steps.pick: Choose the location and the Date above the sheet.
steps.counts: The cards show how many people are In now, Late and Absent.
steps.status: Each row shows the rostered shift, the In and Out times, the Hours worked and a status such as On time, Late, Absent, Due or Not rostered.

staffShifts.title: Shifts and the cash drawer
staffShifts.intro: Shifts has two tabs: the weekly work Roster, and the Cash drawer shift on the till you're using. Open it from Staff → Shifts.

roster.title: Plan the weekly roster

steps.open: Open Staff → Shifts. The Roster tab shows each employee at the location with a shift for every day of the week.
steps.week: Choose the location, and use the arrows beside Week of to move between weeks.
steps.assign: Click a day for an employee and choose a shift (for example Morning or Evening, with its hours) or Off. It saves straight away.

roster.note: Attendance uses the roster to decide who is late or absent.

cashMoves.title: Record cash in or out of the drawer

steps.open: On a till, open Staff → Shifts and click the Cash drawer tab.
steps.summary: The open shift shows the Opening float, Cash sales, Cash refunds, each cash movement, and the Expected in drawer total.
steps.record: Choose Cash out or Cash in, enter the Amount and What for (for example, milk bought for the kitchen).
steps.save: Click Record. The movement is added to the list and the expected total updates.

cashMoves.note: You can't take out more cash than is expected in the drawer. The cash drawer only works on a till that is set up as a device for this location.

steps.count: Under Count and close, count the cash and enter the total in Counted. The screen shows whether the drawer is Balanced, short or over.
steps.close: Click Close shift. The shift moves to Shift history with its expected cash, the count and the Variance.

openShift.title: Open the drawer for a new shift

steps.float: When no shift is open, the tab shows Open the cash drawer. The Opening float starts at what the last person counted when they closed.
steps.pin: Check the float and enter Your PIN.
steps.open: Click Open shift.

openShift.note: Only someone who works at this location can open or close its drawer with their PIN.

staffMeals.title: Staff meals
staffMeals.intro: Record food eaten by staff. No payment is taken, but the food leaves stock like a sale and its value counts against the employee's monthly food allowance. Open it from Staff → Staff Meals.

record.title: Record a staff meal

steps.open: Open Staff → Staff Meals and click Record staff meal.
steps.items: Choose an Item, set the quantity and click Add. Repeat for each item. Use the bin icon to remove one.
steps.approve: Click Record (it shows the total value). A manager enters their PIN, chooses a reason such as Staff meal or Meal on shift, and clicks Confirm.

record.note: Meals are valued at the item's selling price at this location.

steps.list: The list shows each meal, who ate it, the items, where it was recorded (Staff meals or POS), which manager approved it, and the value.
steps.filter: Choose the location and use the arrows to move between months. The top card shows the month's total value and number of meals.
steps.allowance: Click See who's over to open the food allowance for the same month.

staffAllowance.title: Food allowance
staffAllowance.intro: Each employee has a monthly food allowance. This page compares it with what they ate as staff meals, and anything over goes to salary deduction. Open it from Staff → Food Allowance.

steps.open: Open Staff → Food Allowance. The cards show total Allowances, what was Eaten in the month, and the total For salary deduction, with who is over.
steps.month: Use the arrows to choose the month.
steps.read: Each row shows the employee's Monthly food allowance, what they ate (Eaten, with the number of meals), what is Left, and the amount to Deduct from salary.
steps.copy: Click Copy for payroll, then paste into your payroll sheet.

steps.open: Click the employee's name to open their record, then click Edit.

reports.title: Reports
reports.intro: Reports show how the business is doing: sales, products, locations, stock, discounts and voids, and a full history of important changes. Owners and managers find them under Reports in the sidebar. Every report can be downloaded as a CSV file or printed.

salesSummary.title: Check your sales for a period
salesSummary.intro: The Sales summary shows net POS sales: orders count on the day they were paid, and refunds count on the day they were refunded.

steps.open: Open Reports → Sales. The report opens on the Last 7 days. The cards at the top show Net sales, Orders, Average order, Discounts and Refunds.
steps.period: To change the period, pick Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days or This month. You can also set your own dates in From and To.
steps.location: To see one outlet only, choose it in the location list. Keep All locations to see the whole business.
steps.breakdowns: Scroll down to see sales By payment method, By order type, By cashier and Sales by hour. Hover over a bar in a chart to see that day's or hour's sales.
steps.addUp: How net sales add up goes from gross sales to Net sales: discounts come off, service charges and tax are added, and refunds come off. Other channels shows wholesale invoices and staff meals, which are not POS sales.
steps.export: Click Download CSV to save the report as a spreadsheet file, or Print to print it. The filters and buttons are left off the printout.

salesSummary.note: The start date can't be after the end date, and the period can't end after today. If it does, the app asks you to check the dates and doesn't show the report.

steps.open: Open Reports → Product Sales and pick a period. The cards show Net sales, Units sold, Units returned and Discounts, and the chart shows the Top 10 by net sales.
steps.category: To look at one group of products, choose it in the category list. Choose All categories to see everything again.
steps.table: Scroll down to the table. For each product you see units Sold and Returned, the Gross amount, Discounts, the Net amount after discounts and refunds, and its Share of net sales.
steps.export: Click Download CSV for the full list, including net quantity and refunded amounts.

locationSales.title: Compare your locations

steps.open: Open Reports → Location Sales and pick a period.
steps.compare: The table puts each outlet side by side with its Net sales, Orders, Avg order, Discounts, Refunds and Share of POS sales. The POS total is shown under the table.
steps.trend: Scroll down to see each location's sales by day. All the charts use the same scale, so you can compare them at a glance.

locationSales.note: Vans are marked Wholesale. Their invoices are listed apart and are not part of the POS total or share.

stockReport.title: Check stock movement

steps.open: Open Reports → Inventory and pick a period and location. The cards show how many units were Received, Sold, Wasted and used for Staff meals.
steps.columns: Each row is one item at one location. It shows the Opening stock, what came In, what was Sold, Wasted, used for Staff meals or went out in other ways, any Adjusted amount, and the Closing stock.
steps.filter: To see only items that need attention, click Low now or Out now. You can also choose a category.
steps.export: Click Download CSV for the full detail, with received, produced, returned and transferred amounts in their own columns.

stockReport.note: In means received, produced and returned. Other out means used in production or recipes and transferred out. The Status column shows the stock level right now, not at the end of the period.

voids.title: Review discounts, voids and refunds
voids.intro: This report lists every discount, price change, removed item, cancelled order, voided invoice and refund, with who approved it and why.

steps.open: Open Reports → Voids & Discounts and pick a period. The cards show the total and the number of times for each kind.
steps.tabs: Use the tabs to switch between Discounts, Cancelled, Voided, Removed items and Refunds.
steps.rows: Each row shows what happened, when and where, the Reason, the person who approved it with their PIN (Approved by), the cashier who rang it up, and the Amount. Price changes are marked Price.
steps.summary: Scroll to the bottom to see the totals By reason and By approving employee. Use these to spot unusual patterns.

voids.note: Click Download CSV to save every row from all five tabs in one file.

audit.title: See who did what in the audit log
audit.intro: The audit log keeps a record of every important change: who did it, who approved it with a PIN, and why. Records are never edited or deleted.

steps.open: Open Reports → Audit. The newest changes are at the top, with When, the Action, What changed, who it was Done by and, if a PIN was needed, who it was Approved by.
steps.filter: To narrow the list, click an area such as Sales, Inventory or Customers, choose a location, or pick a time such as Today or Last 7 days. You can also type in Search changes, people or reasons.
steps.pin: To see only actions that needed a manager's PIN, click PIN-approved only. To see what one person approved, choose them in the Any approver list. PIN-approved actions have a green shield next to them.
steps.details: Click a row to open its details: when it happened, who did it, who approved it, the reason and where it happened.
steps.changes: When a record was edited, Change details shows each field with its value Before and After the change.
steps.export: Click Download CSV to save all the changes that match your filters, or Print to print the list.
